newsitem.title: USA: AT&T names Donnelley's Walter president.
newsitem.headline: AT&T names Donnelley's Walter president.

text.p: AT&T Corp ended weeks of speculation on Wednesday and named R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co chairman John Walter as president and eventual successor to Robert Allen as chairman.
In an unexpected announcement, the company said Walter has been named president, chief operating officer and board member effective November 1.
Allen said in a statement that AT&T intends to split the chairman and chief executive officer posts in January 1998, and Walter will succeed Allen as chairman at the annual meeting later that year.

AT&T said its board elected Walter unanimously at a special meeting Tuesday evening. It said the board considered "a number of outstanding candidates" but focused on John Walter "because his track record fit so well with the challenges at AT&T."

"The board and I have every expectation that John will become chairman and CEO of AT&T. We intend to split the CEO and chairman roles in January 1998, and I would expect John to succeed me as chairman at the AT&T annual meeting later that year," Allen said in a statement. "In the meantime, we're going to dive into the work ahead of us."
The president and COO post was left vacant after Alex Mandl resigned in August to head a small, new wireless company, Associated Communications.
Expectation of an earlier end to Allen's career had been fanned by the company's profit warning in September.
But analysts had speculated that Allen would surrender the role of chief executive, rather than chairman, to the new candidate and retain his chairmanship until nearer retirement.
The company reported third quarter earnings last week of $0.84 per share, which were in line with analysts' estimates as revised after the September warning.

The third quarter earnings per share declined 12 percent from $0.96 a year ago, with increased competition and higher marketing expenses hitting long distance while financial services sank into losses.

"I'm confident John Walter brings leadership qualities that will make the new AT&T successful, not only in the hotly contested long distance market, but across the whole range of rapidly growing communications services," Allen said in the statement. He added that Walter had "transformed a large, old-line company challenged by new technologies and changing markets into a tough global competitor."
AT&T did not indicate how long Allen will retain the CEO post, or whether Walter was in line to succeed him in that position later.
